scope: English text lessons and local practice only

levels.title: Express yourself flexibly
levels.subtitle: Nuance · Written language · Putting it together

lessons.title: Call me when you get home

grammar.title: Introducing with 是
grammar.vi: I am Vietnamese.
grammar.note: 是 links a subject to a noun identifying it. Do not add 是 before an ordinary descriptive adjective.

grammar.title: Yes–no questions
grammar.vi: Are you a student?
grammar.note: Keep statement word order and add 吗 at the end. Do not add it when the sentence already has a question word.

grammar.title: Negation with 不
grammar.vi: I do not drink coffee.
grammar.note: 不 usually negates habits, intentions, or states. Negating a completed event usually requires 没.

grammar.title: Asking in return with 呢
grammar.vi: I am well. How about you?
grammar.note: 呢 asks about a topic already clear from context. It cannot replace 吗 in every question.

grammar.title: Saying your name
grammar.vi: My name is Xiaoming.
grammar.note: Use 叫 for a personal name. Questions about a surname use 贵姓 or 姓什么, depending on politeness.

grammar.title: Possession with 的
grammar.vi: This is my book.
grammar.note: 的 connects a possessor and a noun. It may be omitted in close relationships such as 我妈妈, but not arbitrarily.

grammar.title: Having and not having
grammar.vi: I have an older sister.
grammar.note: Negate 有 with 没有, never 不有. The spoken tone of 一 can change within a phrase.

grammar.title: Asking about a small quantity
grammar.vi: How many books do you have?
grammar.note: 几 generally asks about an expected small quantity. Use the appropriate measure word.

grammar.title: Asking who
grammar.formula: 谁 in the position of the unknown person
grammar.vi: Who is your teacher?
grammar.note: Keep the question word where the missing information belongs. Both shéi and shuí are accepted readings of 谁.

grammar.title: Asking which
grammar.vi: Which book do you like?
grammar.note: 哪 asks for a choice. Distinguish 哪 nǎ from 那 nà, meaning “that”.

grammar.title: Asking how much
grammar.vi: How much is this apple?
grammar.note: 多少 asks about quantity or price. In price questions, 钱 can immediately follow 多少.

grammar.title: Describing a quality
grammar.vi: The weather is nice today.
grammar.note: 很 often links a subject and adjective without strongly meaning “very”. Do not add 是 before 很好.

grammar.title: Saying where something is
grammar.vi: I am at school.
grammar.note: 在 here expresses location. Distinguish it from 在 before a verb for an ongoing action.

grammar.title: Wanting to do something
grammar.vi: I would like to drink tea.
grammar.note: 想 generally expresses a softer desire than 要. With a person as its object, 想 can mean “miss”.

grammar.title: Talking about likes
grammar.vi: I like watching films.
grammar.note: An activity can follow 喜欢. Do not insert 是 between the subject and 喜欢.

grammar.title: Also
grammar.vi: She also likes music.
grammar.note: 也 normally comes before the verb or adjective, not after the object.

grammar.title: All
grammar.vi: We can all speak Chinese.
grammar.note: 都 covers the previously mentioned group. 都不 and 不都 have different scopes of negation.

grammar.title: Joining nouns
grammar.vi: You and I are going to the park.
grammar.note: 和 normally joins nouns. It does not freely join independent clauses like English “and”.

grammar.title: This and that
grammar.formula: 这 / 那 + measure word + noun
grammar.pinyin: Zhè běn shū hěn yǒu yìsi.
grammar.vi: This book is interesting.
grammar.note: 这 means “this”; 那 means “that”. A countable noun usually needs a measure word.

grammar.title: Numbers and measure words
grammar.vi: I am buying two cups of tea.
grammar.note: Use 两 before many measure words when counting two items. 杯 counts cups; 本 counts books.

grammar.title: Placing time expressions
grammar.vi: I am going to Beijing tomorrow.
grammar.note: Time usually precedes the verb and may also open the sentence. This ordering exercise asks for the subject first.

grammar.title: Days of the week
grammar.vi: What day is it today?
grammar.note: 星期一 is Monday; 星期日 and 星期天 mean Sunday. 是 can sometimes be omitted in time statements.

grammar.title: A learned skill
grammar.vi: I can write Chinese characters.
grammar.note: 会 expresses a learned skill, and sometimes a prediction. Ability depending on circumstances often uses 能.

grammar.title: Ability and circumstances
grammar.vi: Can you come today?
grammar.note: 能 concerns the ability or circumstances to perform an action, rather than only a learned skill.

grammar.title: Wanting or needing
grammar.vi: I would like a bowl of noodles.
grammar.note: 要 is common in orders and requests. 不要 can mean “do not” or “do not want”, depending on context.

grammar.title: Asking permission with 可以
grammar.vi: May I sit here?
grammar.note: 可以 often expresses permission. 不可以 denies permission; 不会 means lacking a skill or predicts that something will not happen.

grammar.title: An action in progress
grammar.vi: She is cooking.
grammar.note: 正在 emphasizes an ongoing action. Do not use it for every static state, such as possession with 有.

grammar.title: A completed action
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le sān běn shū.
grammar.vi: I bought three books.
grammar.note: 了 after a verb marks completion. It is not a universal past-tense marker.

grammar.title: An action that did not happen
grammar.vi: I did not go to school yesterday.
grammar.note: 没 negates the occurrence of an action. The completed-action 了 is usually absent in this negative pattern.

grammar.title: Past experience
grammar.vi: I have been to Shanghai.
grammar.note: 过 expresses prior experience, rather than simply one specific event. Negate it with 没有 + verb + 过.

grammar.title: Earlier than expected
grammar.pinyin: Tā liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
grammar.vi: He was up as early as six.
grammar.note: 就 here suggests earlier than expected. Its meaning depends on context.

grammar.title: Later than expected
grammar.vi: He did not get up until ten.
grammar.note: 才 emphasizes lateness or a condition that must first be met. Compare it with 就 in the same context.

grammar.title: Comparing with 比
grammar.vi: Today is colder than yesterday.
grammar.note: Do not put 很 directly before the adjective in this comparison. A difference in degree can follow the adjective.

grammar.title: Even more
grammar.pinyin: Zhè běn shū gèng yǒu yìsi.
grammar.vi: This book is more interesting.
grammar.note: 更 needs a comparison point in the sentence or context. It is not a standalone noun.

grammar.title: The highest degree
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan zhè shǒu gē.
grammar.vi: I like this song best.
grammar.note: 最 precedes the quality or mental-state verb being emphasized. The comparison group may be implicit.

grammar.title: A little
grammar.vi: Please speak a little more slowly.
grammar.note: 一点儿 follows an adjective to adjust degree. 有点儿 comes before an adjective and means “a little”.

grammar.title: Somewhat
grammar.vi: It is a little cold today.
grammar.note: 有点儿 often describes a less desirable impression. Do not swap its position with 一点儿 in requests.

grammar.title: So…!
grammar.vi: This dish is so spicy.
grammar.note: The final 了 belongs to this exclamation; it does not mark past time.

grammar.title: Cause and result
grammar.formula: 因为 + cause， 所以 + result
grammar.zh: 因为下雨，所以我没出去。
grammar.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ méi chūqù.
grammar.vi: Because it is raining, I am not going out.
grammar.note: Chinese can use both 因为 and 所以. Put the cause before the result in this exercise.

grammar.title: Expressing contrast
grammar.formula: Clause A， 但是 + clause B
grammar.zh: 这件衣服很好看，但是太贵了。
grammar.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu hěn hǎokàn, dànshì tài guì le.
grammar.vi: These clothes look nice, but they are too expensive.
grammar.note: 但是 connects contrasting ideas. 可是 and 不过 offer related meanings with different nuances.

grammar.title: A condition and its result
grammar.zh: 如果明天下雨，我们就不去。
grammar.pinyin: Rúguǒ míngtiān xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù bú qù.
grammar.vi: If it rains tomorrow, we will not go.
grammar.note: 如果 introduces a hypothetical condition. 就 usually follows the subject in the result clause.

grammar.title: Two simultaneous actions
grammar.formula: 一边 + V1， 一边 + V2
grammar.zh: 她一边听音乐，一边做饭。
grammar.pinyin: Tā yìbiān tīng yīnyuè, yìbiān zuò fàn.
grammar.vi: She listens to music while cooking.
grammar.note: Use this pattern for actions that can happen together, not consecutive actions.

grammar.title: Doing things in sequence
grammar.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān chī fàn, zài xuéxí.
grammar.vi: Let’s eat first, then study.
grammar.note: 再 marks the next step here. 又 often describes a repetition that has already happened.

grammar.title: Describing how an action is done
grammar.vi: She speaks very clearly.
grammar.note: 得 links a verb to a description of its performance. Distinguish it from possessive 的 and adverbial 地.

grammar.title: An adverbial with 地
grammar.vi: He studies seriously.
grammar.note: 地 follows an adverbial and precedes the verb. Some adverbials can omit it; not every manner expression needs it.

grammar.title: A continuing state
grammar.vi: The door is open.
grammar.note: 着 emphasizes a maintained state. 正在 instead highlights an action in progress.

grammar.title: Handling a specific object
grammar.formula: Subject + 把 + known object + verb + result
grammar.vi: Please close the door.
grammar.note: 把 usually requires a known object and a result or other complement. It cannot simply be added to every SVO sentence.

grammar.title: The 被 passive
grammar.zh: 我的自行车被弟弟骑走了。
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ de zìxíngchē bèi dìdi qí zǒu le.
grammar.vi: My younger brother rode away on my bicycle.
grammar.note: 被 makes the affected object the topic. The agent may be omitted when unimportant.

grammar.title: Finishing an action
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng kàn wán zhè běn shū le.
grammar.vi: I have finished reading this book.
grammar.note: 完 marks completion of an action. 看了 alone does not necessarily mean reading the whole book.

grammar.title: Reaching a result
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ zhōngyú mǎi dào piào le.
grammar.vi: I finally managed to buy a ticket.
grammar.note: 到 after a verb marks achieving a goal. Before a place, 到 can mean “arrive at”.

grammar.title: A successful perception
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ tīng jiàn le nǐ de shēngyīn.
grammar.vi: I heard your voice.
grammar.note: 听 is listening; 听见 is successfully hearing. Compare 看 with 看见 in the same way.

grammar.title: Done and ready
grammar.vi: The meal is ready.
grammar.note: 好 here marks a satisfactory or ready result, not simply the independent adjective “good”.

grammar.title: Moving outward
grammar.vi: Please take the book out.
grammar.note: 来 usually moves toward the speaker’s viewpoint; 去 moves away. Read the location context.

grammar.title: Beginning an action
grammar.vi: Everyone burst out laughing.
grammar.note: 起来 can mark a beginning or upward movement. Do not always translate it literally as “up”.

grammar.title: Continuing an action
grammar.vi: Please keep speaking.
grammar.note: 下去 can express continuation from now onward. 下来 has different directional or resulting-state uses.

grammar.title: Being able to understand
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ tīng de dǒng zhè duàn lùyīn.
grammar.vi: I can understand this recording.
grammar.note: 得 in a potential complement differs from 得 describing performance. 听不懂 is its usual negative form.

grammar.title: Being unable to finish
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ chī bu liǎo zhème duō.
grammar.vi: I cannot finish eating this much.
grammar.note: 了 in this potential complement is pronounced liǎo, not the particle le.

grammar.title: Emphasizing a known past detail
grammar.vi: I arrived yesterday.
grammar.note: 是…的 highlights the time, place, or manner of a known event. It is not a general future pattern.

grammar.title: Distance
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn jìn.
grammar.vi: My home is very close to school.
grammar.note: 离 expresses distance. Do not insert 在 before 离 in this pattern.

grammar.title: From… to…
grammar.formula: 从 + starting point + 到 + endpoint
grammar.zh: 从这里到车站要十分钟。
grammar.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ dào chēzhàn yào shí fēnzhōng.
grammar.vi: It takes ten minutes from here to the station.
grammar.note: Use this for places or times. The order of the two endpoints matters.

grammar.title: Although
grammar.formula: 虽然 + A， 但是 + B
grammar.zh: 虽然很累，但是他还在学习。
grammar.pinyin: Suīrán hěn lèi, dànshì tā hái zài xuéxí.
grammar.vi: Although he is tired, he is still studying.
grammar.note: 虽然 acknowledges a fact; the next clause goes against expectations. One connector can sometimes be omitted.

grammar.title: Not only… but also…
grammar.formula: 不但 + A， 而且 + B
grammar.zh: 她不但会唱歌，而且会跳舞。
grammar.pinyin: Tā búdàn huì chàng gē, érqiě huì tiào wǔ.
grammar.vi: She can not only sing but also dance.
grammar.note: The clauses add information rather than contrast. The position of 不但 changes when subjects differ.

grammar.title: A sufficient condition
grammar.pinyin: Zhǐyào yǒu shíjiān, wǒ jiù qù.
grammar.vi: As long as I have time, I will go.
grammar.note: 只要 states a sufficient condition. 只有 introduces a necessary condition.

grammar.title: A necessary condition
grammar.vi: Only by working hard can you improve.
grammar.note: Pair 只有 with 才 in this pattern. Do not substitute 就 from the 只要 pattern.

grammar.title: Even…
grammar.formula: 连 + surprising example + 都 + predicate
grammar.zh: 他连自己的生日都忘了。
grammar.pinyin: Tā lián zìjǐ de shēngrì dōu wàng le.
grammar.vi: He even forgot his own birthday.
grammar.note: 连 introduces a surprising case; 都 or 也 marks its inclusion.

grammar.title: The more… the more…
grammar.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yuè kàn yuè yǒu yìsi.
grammar.vi: The more I read this book, the more interesting it becomes.
grammar.note: Two changes in degree are linked. Do not add 很 immediately after 越.

grammar.title: More and more
grammar.pinyin: Tiānqì yuè lái yuè lěng le.
grammar.vi: The weather is getting colder.
grammar.note: This expresses change over time. It does not require two linked factors like 越…越….

grammar.title: Both qualities
grammar.zh: 这个地方既安静，又方便。
grammar.pinyin: Zhège dìfang jì ānjìng, yòu fāngbiàn.
grammar.vi: This place is both quiet and convenient.
grammar.note: 既…又… presents two simultaneous qualities and is often more formal than 又…又….

grammar.title: Two qualities together
grammar.formula: 又 + adjective A + 又 + adjective B
grammar.pinyin: Zhège píngguǒ yòu dà yòu tián.
grammar.vi: This apple is both big and sweet.
grammar.note: Use it for coexisting qualities. A standalone 又 can instead mean “again”.

grammar.title: Alternatives in a statement
grammar.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ hē chá huòzhě kāfēi.
grammar.vi: You can have tea or coffee.
grammar.note: 或者 commonly offers alternatives in a statement. Direct choice questions usually use 还是.

grammar.title: A choice question
grammar.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng hē chá háishi kāfēi?
grammar.vi: Would you like tea or coffee?
grammar.note: Do not add 吗 to the end of this direct choice question.

grammar.title: As soon as
grammar.zh: 我一到家就给你打电话。
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ yí dào jiā jiù gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
grammar.vi: I will call you as soon as I get home.
grammar.note: 一…就… links closely consecutive events or a regular response. It differs from simultaneous 一边…一边….

grammar.title: Besides… also…
grammar.formula: 除了 + A + 以外， 还 + B
grammar.zh: 除了中文以外，她还会英语。
grammar.pinyin: Chúle Zhōngwén yǐwài, tā hái huì Yīngyǔ.
grammar.vi: Besides Chinese, she also speaks English.
grammar.note: 还 or 也 indicates that A is included. This differs from an exception followed by 都.

grammar.title: Except for
grammar.formula: 除了 + exception， 其他 + 都 + predicate
grammar.zh: 除了小王，其他人都来了。
grammar.pinyin: Chúle Xiǎo Wáng, qítā rén dōu lái le.
grammar.vi: Except for Xiaowang, everyone else has arrived.
grammar.note: 都 marks the remaining group. Context determines whether A is excluded.

grammar.title: From someone’s perspective
grammar.zh: 对我来说，这个问题很重要。
grammar.pinyin: Duì wǒ lái shuō, zhège wèntí hěn zhòngyào.
grammar.vi: For me, this issue is very important.
grammar.note: This limits a claim to a viewpoint, rather than stating a universal objective fact.

grammar.title: About a topic
grammar.zh: 我想看一本关于历史的书。
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng kàn yì běn guānyú lìshǐ de shū.
grammar.vi: I want to read a book about history.
grammar.note: 关于 introduces a topic. 对于 usually introduces something being evaluated or handled.

grammar.title: Regarding
grammar.zh: 对于这个建议，我没有意见。
grammar.pinyin: Duìyú zhège jiànyì, wǒ méiyǒu yìjiàn.
grammar.vi: I have no objection to this suggestion.
grammar.note: 对于 introduces the object of an attitude or comment. It cannot replace every 关于.

grammar.title: A written cause and result
grammar.formula: 由于 + cause， 因此 + result
grammar.zh: 由于天气不好，因此航班取消了。
grammar.pinyin: Yóuyú tiānqì bù hǎo, yīncǐ hángbān qǔxiāo le.
grammar.vi: The flight was canceled because of bad weather.
grammar.note: 由于 and 因此 are relatively formal. 因此 can be omitted when the relationship is clear.

grammar.title: Even if
grammar.formula: 即使 + hypothetical condition， 也 + result
grammar.pinyin: Jíshǐ xià yǔ, wǒ yě huì qù.
grammar.vi: Even if it rains, I will still go.
grammar.note: 即使 can describe something that has not happened. 虽然 usually acknowledges a known fact.

grammar.title: No matter
grammar.formula: 无论 + question word / alternatives， 都 + result
grammar.zh: 无论你去哪里，我都支持你。
grammar.pinyin: Wúlùn nǐ qù nǎlǐ, wǒ dōu zhīchí nǐ.
grammar.vi: Wherever you go, I will support you.
grammar.note: 无论 needs a range of alternatives or a question word, not just one ordinary affirmative event.

grammar.title: Since… then…
grammar.formula: 既然 + accepted fact， 就 + conclusion
grammar.zh: 既然你知道，就告诉我吧。
grammar.pinyin: Jìrán nǐ zhīdào, jiù gàosu wǒ ba.
grammar.vi: Since you know, please tell me.
grammar.note: 既然 uses an accepted premise to support a conclusion or suggestion, rather than only giving an objective cause.

grammar.title: Adding emphasis with 不仅
grammar.zh: 运动不仅有益健康，还能减轻压力。
grammar.pinyin: Yùndòng bùjǐn yǒuyì jiànkāng, hái néng jiǎnqīng yālì.
grammar.vi: Exercise not only benefits health but also reduces stress.
grammar.note: The clauses add information. 而且 can also introduce the second clause, depending on structure.

grammar.title: Would rather… than…
grammar.formula: 宁可 + A， 也不 + B
grammar.zh: 我宁可走路，也不等这么久。
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ nìngkě zǒu lù, yě bù děng zhème jiǔ.
grammar.vi: I would rather walk than wait this long.
grammar.note: 宁可 states the speaker’s preference. 也不 introduces the rejected alternative.

grammar.title: Rather than… better to…
grammar.formula: 与其 + A， 不如 + B
grammar.vi: Rather than complain, think of a solution.
grammar.note: 与其 introduces the less desirable option; 不如 presents the better choice. Reversing them changes the meaning.

grammar.title: Despite this, still
grammar.formula: 尽管 + fact， 仍然 + result
grammar.zh: 尽管很忙，她仍然每天读书。
grammar.pinyin: Jǐnguǎn hěn máng, tā réngrán měitiān dú shū.
grammar.vi: Despite being busy, she still reads every day.
grammar.note: 尽管 expresses concession here. In other contexts, 你尽管问 means “go ahead and ask”.

grammar.title: Unless… otherwise…
grammar.formula: 除非 + condition， 否则 + result
grammar.zh: 除非你同意，否则我不去。
grammar.pinyin: Chúfēi nǐ tóngyì, fǒuzé wǒ bú qù.
grammar.vi: Unless you agree, I will not go.
grammar.note: The condition after 除非 is the necessary exception. Read the negation in the 否则 clause carefully.

grammar.title: To avoid
grammar.vi: Please leave early to avoid being late.
grammar.note: 以免 introduces an outcome to avoid. An unnecessary extra negative can reverse the meaning.

grammar.title: To make something easier
grammar.vi: Please leave a phone number so we can contact you.
grammar.note: 以便 introduces a facilitating purpose, often in instructions or written language.

grammar.title: No wonder
grammar.zh: 难怪他没来，原来生病了。
grammar.pinyin: Nánguài tā méi lái, yuánlái shēng bìng le.
grammar.vi: No wonder he did not come; he was ill.
grammar.note: 难怪 signals that discovering a cause makes a result unsurprising.

grammar.title: Almost
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ chàdiǎnr wàng le dài yàoshi.
grammar.vi: I almost forgot to bring my keys.
grammar.note: 差点儿 usually describes something that nearly happened but did not. Uses with 没 depend on desirability and context.

grammar.title: It turns out
grammar.pinyin: Yuánlái nǐ yě zhù zài zhèlǐ.
grammar.vi: It turns out you live here too.
grammar.note: 原来 can mean “it turns out” or “originally”. Decide from its function in the sentence.

grammar.title: After all / exactly
grammar.formula: Subject + 究竟 + question word / predicate
grammar.vi: What exactly are you trying to say?
grammar.note: 究竟 emphasizes a request for clarification. It can sound insistent, so consider tone and relationship.

grammar.title: Not necessarily
grammar.vi: Expensive things are not necessarily good.
grammar.note: 未必 denies certainty. It does not assert the opposite as certain.

grammar.title: Instead, against expectations
grammar.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu shēng qì, fǎn'ér xiào le.
grammar.vi: He was not angry; instead, he laughed.
grammar.note: 反而 introduces a result contrary to expectations, not just any different piece of information.

grammar.title: Two sides of an issue
grammar.formula: 一方面 + A， 另一方面 + B
grammar.zh: 他一方面想去，另一方面又担心费用。
grammar.pinyin: Tā yì fāngmiàn xiǎng qù, lìng yì fāngmiàn yòu dānxīn fèiyòng.
grammar.vi: On one hand he wants to go; on the other, he worries about the cost.
grammar.note: The two sides may complement or conflict. Use parallel structure for clarity.

grammar.title: In short
grammar.zh: 总之，我们需要继续努力。
grammar.vi: In short, we need to keep trying.
grammar.note: 总之 brings earlier points together. It normally needs preceding explanation or a clear context.

grammar.title: Affirmative–negative questions
grammar.vi: Are you going?
grammar.note: Do not add 吗 to an affirmative–negative question. With 有, use 有没有.

grammar.title: Asking where
grammar.formula: 哪里 in the place position
grammar.vi: Where do you live?
grammar.note: 哪里 and 哪儿 both ask where. Keep the question word in the missing place’s normal position.

grammar.title: Asking how
grammar.vi: How do you write this character?
grammar.note: 怎么 asks how; 为什么 usually asks why. In some contexts 怎么 can ask a surprised “why”.

grammar.title: Asking why
grammar.vi: Why are you learning Chinese?
grammar.note: You can answer with 因为. Do not add 吗 when 为什么 is already present.

grammar.title: Asking when
grammar.vi: When are you going home?
grammar.note: Put the question phrase in the time position. 什么时候 does not ask how long something lasts.

grammar.title: Asking for an opinion
grammar.vi: What do you think of this approach?
grammar.note: 怎么样 asks for an evaluation. 怎么 + verb asks how to do something.

grammar.title: Every…
grammar.formula: 每 + measure word + noun + 都
grammar.pinyin: Měi ge xuésheng dōu yǒu yì běn shū.
grammar.vi: Every student has a book.
grammar.note: 每 usually takes a measure word. Common time expressions 每天 and 每年 do not add 个.

grammar.title: An equal comparison
grammar.formula: A + 跟 + B + 一样 + adjective
grammar.pinyin: Zhè běn shū gēn nà běn yíyàng guì.
grammar.vi: This book is as expensive as that one.
grammar.note: 和 can replace 跟. Do not use 比 to express equality in this pattern.

grammar.title: Not as… as…
grammar.vi: Today is not as hot as yesterday.
grammar.note: 没有 denies reaching B’s degree. 不比 only denies being more and does not always mean being less.

grammar.title: Not at all
grammar.formula: 一点儿 + 也 / 都 + 不 + predicate
grammar.zh: 这个问题一点儿也不难。
grammar.pinyin: Zhège wèntí yìdiǎnr yě bù nán.
grammar.vi: This problem is not difficult at all.
grammar.note: Use 不 for the state in this example. 一点儿也没有 can negate an amount or existence.

grammar.title: A new state with 了
grammar.vi: The weather has turned cold.
grammar.note: Sentence-final 了 can signal a change of state, not necessarily a completed past action.

grammar.title: About to happen
grammar.vi: It is about to rain.
grammar.note: 快要, 就要, and 要…了 express an imminent event. Distinguish this from 要 expressing desire.

grammar.title: Repeating with 再 and 又
grammar.formula: 再 for a future repetition; 又 for one already made
grammar.vi: Please say it once more.
grammar.note: 再 usually looks ahead to a repetition; 又 often refers to one already made. Fixed expressions can behave differently.

grammar.title: Just now
grammar.vi: He has just left.
grammar.note: 刚刚 commonly sits near the verb as an adverb. 刚才 is a time expression with broader noun-phrase uses.

grammar.title: Already
grammar.vi: I have already eaten.
grammar.note: 已经 emphasizes that a state has been reached by the reference time. Whether 了 is needed depends on the construction.

grammar.title: Doing something for someone
grammar.vi: I am calling my mother.
grammar.note: 给 can introduce the recipient of an action. It is also the verb “give”, as in 给你一本书.

grammar.title: Having someone do something
grammar.formula: Person A + 让 + person B + verb
grammar.vi: The teacher asks us to read the text.
grammar.note: 让 can mean letting, allowing, or asking, depending on context. The person doing the action follows 让.

grammar.title: Purpose with 为了
grammar.vi: I exercise every day for my health.
grammar.note: 为了 states an intended purpose; 因为 gives the cause of an event.

grammar.title: Times and complete passes
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ dú le liǎng biàn kèwén.
grammar.vi: I have read the text through twice.
grammar.note: 遍 emphasizes a complete pass from beginning to end; 次 counts occurrences. Object placement depends on the object type.

grammar.title: A duration complement
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ děng le bàn ge xiǎoshí.
grammar.vi: I waited for half an hour.
grammar.note: Duration describes how long an action lasts. A time point such as 三点 normally precedes the verb.

grammar.title: Never / ever
grammar.formula: 从来 + 不 / 没 + verb
grammar.vi: I never drink alcohol.
grammar.note: 从来不 describes a habit; 从来没…过 describes never having had an experience.

grammar.title: Only
grammar.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ yǒu shí kuài qián.
grammar.vi: I only have ten yuan.
grammar.note: 只 limits scope or quantity. Its position determines what is limited.

grammar.title: An extreme degree
grammar.vi: It is incredibly hot today.
grammar.note: 不得了 is an emphatic degree complement here, often conversational. It is not the potential complement “cannot do”.

grammar.title: Resembling
grammar.zh: 她的声音像妈妈的声音。
grammar.pinyin: Tā de shēngyīn xiàng māma de shēngyīn.
grammar.vi: Her voice sounds like her mother’s.
grammar.note: 像 is the verb “resemble”. 一样 can extend the comparison; 是 is not needed before 像.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 是 + noun
exercises.explanation: 我是越南人。 I am Vietnamese. 是 links a subject to a noun identifying it. Do not add 是 before an ordinary descriptive adjective.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Statement + 吗
exercises.explanation: 你是学生吗？ Are you a student? Keep statement word order and add 吗 at the end. Do not add it when the sentence already has a question word.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 不 + verb / adjective
exercises.explanation: 我不喝咖啡。 I do not drink coffee. 不 usually negates habits, intentions, or states. Negating a completed event usually requires 没.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Topic + 呢
exercises.explanation: 我很好，你呢？ I am well. How about you? 呢 asks about a topic already clear from context. It cannot replace 吗 in every question.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 叫 + name
exercises.explanation: 我叫小明。 My name is Xiaoming. Use 叫 for a personal name. Questions about a surname use 贵姓 or 姓什么, depending on politeness.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Possessor + 的 + noun
exercises.explanation: 这是我的书。 This is my book. 的 connects a possessor and a noun. It may be omitted in close relationships such as 我妈妈, but not arbitrarily.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Type the Chinese word meaning “be called”.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 有 + object
exercises.explanation: 我有一个姐姐。 I have an older sister. Negate 有 with 没有, never 不有. The spoken tone of 一 can change within a phrase.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 几 + measure word + noun
exercises.explanation: 你有几本书？ How many books do you have? 几 generally asks about an expected small quantity. Use the appropriate measure word.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Type the Chinese word meaning “older sister”.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 谁 in the position of the unknown person
exercises.explanation: 谁是你的老师？ Who is your teacher? Keep the question word where the missing information belongs. Both shéi and shuí are accepted readings of 谁.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 哪 + measure word + noun
exercises.explanation: 你喜欢哪本书？ Which book do you like? 哪 asks for a choice. Distinguish 哪 nǎ from 那 nà, meaning “that”.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Noun / topic + 多少
exercises.explanation: 这个苹果多少钱？ How much is this apple? 多少 asks about quantity or price. In price questions, 钱 can immediately follow 多少.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 很 + adjective
exercises.explanation: 今天的天气很好。 The weather is nice today. 很 often links a subject and adjective without strongly meaning “very”. Do not add 是 before 很好.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 在 + place
exercises.explanation: 我在学校。 I am at school. 在 here expresses location. Distinguish it from 在 before a verb for an ongoing action.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 想 + verb
exercises.explanation: 我想喝茶。 I would like to drink tea. 想 generally expresses a softer desire than 要. With a person as its object, 想 can mean “miss”.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 喜欢 + noun / verb
exercises.explanation: 我喜欢看电影。 I like watching films. An activity can follow 喜欢. Do not insert 是 between the subject and 喜欢.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 也 + predicate
exercises.explanation: 她也喜欢音乐。 She also likes music. 也 normally comes before the verb or adjective, not after the object.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Plural subject + 都 + predicate
exercises.explanation: 我们都会说中文。 We can all speak Chinese. 都 covers the previously mentioned group. 都不 and 不都 have different scopes of negation.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Noun A + 和 + noun B
exercises.explanation: 我和朋友去公园。 You and I are going to the park. 和 normally joins nouns. It does not freely join independent clauses like English “and”.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 这 / 那 + measure word + noun
exercises.explanation: 这本书很有意思。 This book is interesting. 这 means “this”; 那 means “that”. A countable noun usually needs a measure word.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Number + measure word + noun
exercises.explanation: 我买两杯茶。 I am buying two cups of tea. Use 两 before many measure words when counting two items. 杯 counts cups; 本 counts books.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + time + verb
exercises.explanation: 我明天去北京。 I am going to Beijing tomorrow. Time usually precedes the verb and may also open the sentence. This ordering exercise asks for the subject first.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 今天 + 星期几
exercises.explanation: 今天是星期几？ What day is it today? 星期一 is Monday; 星期日 and 星期天 mean Sunday. 是 can sometimes be omitted in time statements.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 会 + verb
exercises.explanation: 我会写汉字。 I can write Chinese characters. 会 expresses a learned skill, and sometimes a prediction. Ability depending on circumstances often uses 能.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 能 + verb
exercises.explanation: 你今天能来吗？ Can you come today? 能 concerns the ability or circumstances to perform an action, rather than only a learned skill.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
exercises.explanation: You heard 汉字 (Hànzì): Chinese characters.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 要 + noun / verb
exercises.explanation: 我要一碗面条。 I would like a bowl of noodles. 要 is common in orders and requests. 不要 can mean “do not” or “do not want”, depending on context.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 可以 + verb + 吗
exercises.explanation: 我可以坐这里吗？ May I sit here? 可以 often expresses permission. 不可以 denies permission; 不会 means lacking a skill or predicts that something will not happen.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 正在 + verb
exercises.explanation: 她正在做饭。 She is cooking. 正在 emphasizes an ongoing action. Do not use it for every static state, such as possession with 有.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Verb + 了 + object
exercises.explanation: 我买了三本书。 I bought three books. 了 after a verb marks completion. It is not a universal past-tense marker.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.

exercises.explanation: 去过 (qù guo): have been to.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 没 + verb
exercises.explanation: 我昨天没去学校。 I did not go to school yesterday. 没 negates the occurrence of an action. The completed-action 了 is usually absent in this negative pattern.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Verb + 过 + object
exercises.explanation: 我去过上海。 I have been to Shanghai. 过 expresses prior experience, rather than simply one specific event. Negate it with 没有 + verb + 过.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Time / condition + 就 + verb
exercises.explanation: 他六点就起床了。 He was up as early as six. 就 here suggests earlier than expected. Its meaning depends on context.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Time + 才 + verb
exercises.explanation: 他十点才起床。 He did not get up until ten. 才 emphasizes lateness or a condition that must first be met. Compare it with 就 in the same context.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
exercises.explanation: You heard 十点 (shí diǎn): ten o’clock.

exercises.prompt: Type the Chinese word meaning “six o’clock”.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: A + 比 + B + adjective
exercises.explanation: 今天比昨天冷。 Today is colder than yesterday. Do not put 很 directly before the adjective in this comparison. A difference in degree can follow the adjective.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 更 + adjective
exercises.explanation: 这本书更有意思。 This book is more interesting. 更 needs a comparison point in the sentence or context. It is not a standalone noun.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Scope + 最 + adjective
exercises.explanation: 我最喜欢这首歌。 I like this song best. 最 precedes the quality or mental-state verb being emphasized. The comparison group may be implicit.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Adjective + 一点儿
exercises.explanation: 请说慢一点儿。 Please speak a little more slowly. 一点儿 follows an adjective to adjust degree. 有点儿 comes before an adjective and means “a little”.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 有点儿 + adjective
exercises.explanation: 今天有点儿冷。 It is a little cold today. 有点儿 often describes a less desirable impression. Do not swap its position with 一点儿 in requests.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 太 + adjective + 了
exercises.explanation: 这个菜太辣了。 This dish is so spicy. The final 了 belongs to this exclamation; it does not mark past time.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 因为 + cause， 所以 + result
exercises.answer: 因为下雨，所以我没出去
exercises.explanation: 因为下雨，所以我没出去。 Because it is raining, I am not going out. Chinese can use both 因为 and 所以. Put the cause before the result in this exercise.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Clause A， 但是 + clause B
exercises.answer: 这件衣服很好看，但是太贵了
exercises.explanation: 这件衣服很好看，但是太贵了。 These clothes look nice, but they are too expensive. 但是 connects contrasting ideas. 可是 and 不过 offer related meanings with different nuances.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
exercises.explanation: You heard 出去 (chūqù): go out.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 如果 + condition， 就 + result
exercises.answer: 如果明天下雨，我们就不去
exercises.explanation: 如果明天下雨，我们就不去。 If it rains tomorrow, we will not go. 如果 introduces a hypothetical condition. 就 usually follows the subject in the result clause.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 一边 + V1， 一边 + V2
exercises.answer: 她一边听音乐，一边做饭
exercises.explanation: 她一边听音乐，一边做饭。 She listens to music while cooking. Use this pattern for actions that can happen together, not consecutive actions.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 先 + V1， 再 + V2
exercises.explanation: 我们先吃饭，再学习。 Let’s eat first, then study. 再 marks the next step here. 又 often describes a repetition that has already happened.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Verb + 得 + description
exercises.explanation: 她说得很清楚。 She speaks very clearly. 得 links a verb to a description of its performance. Distinguish it from possessive 的 and adverbial 地.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Description + 地 + verb
exercises.explanation: 他认真地学习。 He studies seriously. 地 follows an adverbial and precedes the verb. Some adverbials can omit it; not every manner expression needs it.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Verb + 着
exercises.explanation: 门开着。 The door is open. 着 emphasizes a maintained state. 正在 instead highlights an action in progress.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Type the Chinese word meaning “serious; conscientious”.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 把 + known object + verb + result
exercises.explanation: 请把门关上。 Please close the door. 把 usually requires a known object and a result or other complement. It cannot simply be added to every SVO sentence.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Affected object + 被 + agent + action
exercises.answer: 我的自行车被弟弟骑走了
exercises.explanation: 我的自行车被弟弟骑走了。 My younger brother rode away on my bicycle. 被 makes the affected object the topic. The agent may be omitted when unimportant.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Verb + 完
exercises.explanation: 我已经看完这本书了。 I have finished reading this book. 完 marks completion of an action. 看了 alone does not necessarily mean reading the whole book.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Verb + 到
exercises.explanation: 我终于买到票了。 I finally managed to buy a ticket. 到 after a verb marks achieving a goal. Before a place, 到 can mean “arrive at”.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 看 / 听 + 见
exercises.explanation: 我听见了你的声音。 I heard your voice. 听 is listening; 听见 is successfully hearing. Compare 看 with 看见 in the same way.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Verb + 好
exercises.explanation: 饭已经做好了。 The meal is ready. 好 here marks a satisfactory or ready result, not simply the independent adjective “good”.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Verb + 出来
exercises.explanation: 请把书拿出来。 Please take the book out. 来 usually moves toward the speaker’s viewpoint; 去 moves away. Read the location context.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Verb + 起来
exercises.explanation: 大家都笑起来了。 Everyone burst out laughing. 起来 can mark a beginning or upward movement. Do not always translate it literally as “up”.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Type the Chinese word meaning “take; hold”.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Verb + 下去
exercises.explanation: 请继续说下去。 Please keep speaking. 下去 can express continuation from now onward. 下来 has different directional or resulting-state uses.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Verb + 得 + complement
exercises.explanation: 我听得懂这段录音。 I can understand this recording. 得 in a potential complement differs from 得 describing performance. 听不懂 is its usual negative form.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Verb + 不 + 了
exercises.explanation: 我吃不了这么多。 I cannot finish eating this much. 了 in this potential complement is pronounced liǎo, not the particle le.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 是 + detail + verb + 的
exercises.explanation: 我是昨天来的。 I arrived yesterday. 是…的 highlights the time, place, or manner of a known event. It is not a general future pattern.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
exercises.explanation: You heard 这么多 (zhème duō): this much.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: A + 离 + B + far / near
exercises.explanation: 我家离学校很近。 My home is very close to school. 离 expresses distance. Do not insert 在 before 离 in this pattern.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 从 + starting point + 到 + endpoint
exercises.answer: 从这里到车站要十分钟
exercises.explanation: 从这里到车站要十分钟。 It takes ten minutes from here to the station. Use this for places or times. The order of the two endpoints matters.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 虽然 + A， 但是 + B
exercises.answer: 虽然很累，但是他还在学习
exercises.explanation: 虽然很累，但是他还在学习。 Although he is tired, he is still studying. 虽然 acknowledges a fact; the next clause goes against expectations. One connector can sometimes be omitted.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 不但 + A， 而且 + B
exercises.answer: 她不但会唱歌，而且会跳舞
exercises.explanation: 她不但会唱歌，而且会跳舞。 She can not only sing but also dance. The clauses add information rather than contrast. The position of 不但 changes when subjects differ.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
exercises.explanation: You heard 唱歌 (chàng gē): sing.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 只要 + condition， 就 + result
exercises.explanation: 只要有时间，我就去。 As long as I have time, I will go. 只要 states a sufficient condition. 只有 introduces a necessary condition.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 只有 + condition， 才 + result
exercises.explanation: 只有努力，才能进步。 Only by working hard can you improve. Pair 只有 with 才 in this pattern. Do not substitute 就 from the 只要 pattern.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
exercises.explanation: You heard 努力 (nǔlì): make an effort.
越来越 (yuè lái yuè): more and more.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 连 + surprising example + 都 + predicate
exercises.answer: 他连自己的生日都忘了
exercises.explanation: 他连自己的生日都忘了。 He even forgot his own birthday. 连 introduces a surprising case; 都 or 也 marks its inclusion.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 越 + A， 越 + B
exercises.explanation: 这本书越看越有意思。 The more I read this book, the more interesting it becomes. Two changes in degree are linked. Do not add 很 immediately after 越.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 越来越 + adjective
exercises.explanation: 天气越来越冷了。 The weather is getting colder. This expresses change over time. It does not require two linked factors like 越…越….

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 既 + A， 又 + B
exercises.answer: 这个地方既安静，又方便
exercises.explanation: 这个地方既安静，又方便。 This place is both quiet and convenient. 既…又… presents two simultaneous qualities and is often more formal than 又…又….

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 又 + adjective A + 又 + adjective B
exercises.explanation: 这个苹果又大又甜。 This apple is both big and sweet. Use it for coexisting qualities. A standalone 又 can instead mean “again”.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: A + 或者 + B
exercises.explanation: 你可以喝茶或者咖啡。 You can have tea or coffee. 或者 commonly offers alternatives in a statement. Direct choice questions usually use 还是.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: A + 还是 + B
exercises.explanation: 你想喝茶还是咖啡？ Would you like tea or coffee? Do not add 吗 to the end of this direct choice question.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 一 + V1， 就 + V2
exercises.answer: 我一到家就给你打电话
exercises.explanation: 我一到家就给你打电话。 I will call you as soon as I get home. 一…就… links closely consecutive events or a regular response. It differs from simultaneous 一边…一边….

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
exercises.explanation: You heard 到家 (dào jiā): arrive home.

exercises.prompt: Type the Chinese word meaning “or (in a question)”.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 除了 + A + 以外， 还 + B
exercises.answer: 除了中文以外，她还会英语
exercises.explanation: 除了中文以外，她还会英语。 Besides Chinese, she also speaks English. 还 or 也 indicates that A is included. This differs from an exception followed by 都.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 除了 + exception， 其他 + 都 + predicate
exercises.answer: 除了小王，其他人都来了
exercises.explanation: 除了小王，其他人都来了。 Except for Xiaowang, everyone else has arrived. 都 marks the remaining group. Context determines whether A is excluded.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
exercises.explanation: You heard 其他人 (qítā rén): other people.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 对 + person + 来说
exercises.answer: 对我来说，这个问题很重要
exercises.explanation: 对我来说，这个问题很重要。 For me, this issue is very important. This limits a claim to a viewpoint, rather than stating a universal objective fact.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 关于 + topic + 的 + noun
exercises.answer: 我想看一本关于历史的书
exercises.explanation: 我想看一本关于历史的书。 I want to read a book about history. 关于 introduces a topic. 对于 usually introduces something being evaluated or handled.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 对于 + object， subject + predicate
exercises.answer: 对于这个建议，我没有意见
exercises.explanation: 对于这个建议，我没有意见。 I have no objection to this suggestion. 对于 introduces the object of an attitude or comment. It cannot replace every 关于.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 由于 + cause， 因此 + result
exercises.answer: 由于天气不好，因此航班取消了
exercises.explanation: 由于天气不好，因此航班取消了。 The flight was canceled because of bad weather. 由于 and 因此 are relatively formal. 因此 can be omitted when the relationship is clear.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 即使 + hypothetical condition， 也 + result
exercises.explanation: 即使下雨，我也会去。 Even if it rains, I will still go. 即使 can describe something that has not happened. 虽然 usually acknowledges a known fact.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 无论 + question word / alternatives， 都 + result
exercises.answer: 无论你去哪里，我都支持你
exercises.explanation: 无论你去哪里，我都支持你。 Wherever you go, I will support you. 无论 needs a range of alternatives or a question word, not just one ordinary affirmative event.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Type the Chinese word meaning “even if”.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 既然 + accepted fact， 就 + conclusion
exercises.answer: 既然你知道，就告诉我吧
exercises.explanation: 既然你知道，就告诉我吧。 Since you know, please tell me. 既然 uses an accepted premise to support a conclusion or suggestion, rather than only giving an objective cause.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 不仅 + A， 还 + B
exercises.answer: 运动不仅有益健康，还能减轻压力
exercises.explanation: 运动不仅有益健康，还能减轻压力。 Exercise not only benefits health but also reduces stress. The clauses add information. 而且 can also introduce the second clause, depending on structure.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 宁可 + A， 也不 + B
exercises.answer: 我宁可走路，也不等这么久
exercises.explanation: 我宁可走路，也不等这么久。 I would rather walk than wait this long. 宁可 states the speaker’s preference. 也不 introduces the rejected alternative.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 与其 + A， 不如 + B
exercises.explanation: 与其抱怨，不如想办法。 Rather than complain, think of a solution. 与其 introduces the less desirable option; 不如 presents the better choice. Reversing them changes the meaning.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 尽管 + fact， 仍然 + result
exercises.answer: 尽管很忙，她仍然每天读书
exercises.explanation: 尽管很忙，她仍然每天读书。 Despite being busy, she still reads every day. 尽管 expresses concession here. In other contexts, 你尽管问 means “go ahead and ask”.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 除非 + condition， 否则 + result
exercises.answer: 除非你同意，否则我不去
exercises.explanation: 除非你同意，否则我不去。 Unless you agree, I will not go. The condition after 除非 is the necessary exception. Read the negation in the 否则 clause carefully.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
exercises.explanation: You heard 读书 (dú shū): read books.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Action， 以免 + unwanted result
exercises.explanation: 请提前出发，以免迟到。 Please leave early to avoid being late. 以免 introduces an outcome to avoid. An unnecessary extra negative can reverse the meaning.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Action， 以便 + purpose
exercises.explanation: 请留下电话，以便联系。 Please leave a phone number so we can contact you. 以便 introduces a facilitating purpose, often in instructions or written language.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
exercises.explanation: You heard 出发 (chūfā): set off.

exercises.prompt: Type the Chinese word meaning “in advance”.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 难怪 + now-understood result
exercises.answer: 难怪他没来，原来生病了
exercises.explanation: 难怪他没来，原来生病了。 No wonder he did not come; he was ill. 难怪 signals that discovering a cause makes a result unsurprising.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 差点儿 + verb
exercises.explanation: 我差点儿忘了带钥匙。 I almost forgot to bring my keys. 差点儿 usually describes something that nearly happened but did not. Uses with 没 depend on desirability and context.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Type the Chinese word meaning “be ill”.
Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 原来 + newly realized information
exercises.explanation: 原来你也住在这里。 It turns out you live here too. 原来 can mean “it turns out” or “originally”. Decide from its function in the sentence.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Subject + 究竟 + question word / predicate
exercises.explanation: 你究竟想说什么？ What exactly are you trying to say? 究竟 emphasizes a request for clarification. It can sound insistent, so consider tone and relationship.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
Type the Chinese word meaning “it turns out”.

exercises.explanation: 反而 (fǎn'ér): instead; contrary to expectations.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 未必 + predicate
exercises.explanation: 贵的东西未必好。 Expensive things are not necessarily good. 未必 denies certainty. It does not assert the opposite as certain.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: Situation A， 反而 + B
exercises.explanation: 他没有生气，反而笑了。 He was not angry; instead, he laughed. 反而 introduces a result contrary to expectations, not just any different piece of information.

exercises.prompt: Listen and choose the word you hear.
exercises.explanation: You heard 未必 (wèibì): not necessarily.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 一方面 + A， 另一方面 + B
exercises.answer: 他一方面想去，另一方面又担心费用
exercises.explanation: 他一方面想去，另一方面又担心费用。 On one hand he wants to go; on the other, he worries about the cost. The two sides may complement or conflict. Use parallel structure for clarity.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the sentence using this pattern: 总之 + conclusion
exercises.answer: 总之，我们需要继续努力
exercises.explanation: 总之，我们需要继续努力。 In short, we need to keep trying. 总之 brings earlier points together. It normally needs preceding explanation or a clear context.
